headline: OCD: 32 Dead, 8 Million Affected by Habagat and Recent Cyclones
seoTitle: OCD: 32 Dead, 8M Affected by Habagat, Cyclones | FMB News
seoDescription: The Office of Civil Defense reported 32 deaths and around 8 million people affected by Habagat and recent cyclones, with 117 LGUs under a state of calamity.
deck: Around 2.3 million families have been affected, while government assistance has reached about ₱1.65 billion, according to the latest OCD figures.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: At least 32 people have died and around 8 million people, equivalent to about 2.3 million families, have been affected by the combined effects of the Southwest Monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng, according to the Office of Civil Defense.
The OCD also reported 19 injured people and three people still missing. About 25,800 people remained in evacuation centers as of the latest situation report.

sections.heading: Damage and assistance
paragraphs: Infrastructure damage has reached about ₱6.11 billion and agricultural losses about ₱2.32 billion. Nearly 3,000 houses were damaged, including 349 that were totally destroyed.
At least 117 local government units have declared a state of calamity. Government assistance to affected communities has reached about ₱1.65 billion.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The prolonged emergency follows successive tropical cyclones and renewed Habagat rains that have saturated communities across the country, increasing flood and landslide risks even after individual weather systems move away.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The scale of the affected population and infrastructure losses means recovery will extend beyond immediate evacuation and relief distribution. Local governments must also restore transport links, homes, farms and public services while monitoring communities exposed to further rainfall.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated OCD and NDRRMC casualty validation, evacuation-center counts, damage assessments and additional government assistance as weather conditions evolve.
